justification: Judged afresh. The minimal pair is gone and the r3 channel it created is closed. What remains is the second-limb corroboration audit: a careful reader who checks both limbs of each option against the other four questions reaches D without the passage. I measure that at roughly 50 per cent - about twice the 25 per cent baseline - because the audit is two-step and each distractor's first limb is genuinely corroborated, so the reader must get as far as noticing that only D's second limb is echoed. Per the accepted structural finding, this is the floor for a main-idea key on a well-built sheet rather than a defect: any main-idea distractor must name something the text does not centrally do, which on a five-question sheet necessarily makes it the orphan. I am NOT calling for another rebuild on that account. I do report one genuinely new item plainly: the character-length asymmetry introduced when A, B and C were rewritten shorter than the untouched key. It is weak, contradicted by word count, and punished by the rest of the sheet, so it does not change the verdict - but it is new since r3 and the owner should know it exists. Pass.
